pages.alt: A circle standing on the ground, with a diameter across it. It rolls once to the right, and its rim lays down a straight track, its circumference. 3 diameters laid under the track, end to end. With 0.14 of a diameter more, the track is π diameters long, about 3.14: C equals pi times d.

pages.text: Roll a circle once and its rim lays down its [[circumference]]. For every circle it is just over 3 diameters, a number called [[π]], about 3.14. So C = πd.

pages.alt: A pipe's end, a circle 10 centimetres across, standing on the ground. It rolls once and its rim lays down a track 31.42 centimetres long, pi times 10 centimetres.
pages.name: Round a pipe
pages.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 340 210" width="340" style="fill:#1d1f22;stroke:none;stroke-width:1px;font-family:system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-weight:400;text-anchor:start" height="210"><g><line x1="8" y1="200" x2="332" y2="200" style="stroke:#a9afb6;stroke-width:1.5px"/><line x1="46" y1="200" x2="284.76" y2="200" style="stroke:#1d1f22;stroke-width:3px;stroke-linecap:round"/><circle cx="284.76" cy="162" r="38" style="fill:none;stroke:#1d1f22;stroke-width:3px"/><circle cx="284.76" cy="200" r="4.5"/><g><text x="338" y="15" text-anchor="end" style="fill:#0b6a70;stroke:#fff;stroke-width:3.25px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">once round</text><text x="338" y="38" text-anchor="end" style="stroke:#fff;stroke-width:5px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:20px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">π × 10 = 31.42 cm</text></g></g><g/></svg>
pages.task: A pipe is 10 cm across. How far is it round?
pages.why: Across is the diameter, so d = 10 cm. The way round is C = πd = π × 10 = 31.42 cm, just over 3 times across.

pages.alt: A circle cut into 16 wedges, the upper half's and the lower half's in two tints. The wedges are laid top to tail in a rough rectangle, the upper half's rim along its top and the lower half's along its bottom. It is half the circumference long, pi r. It is one radius tall, r. Its area is pi r times r, which is pi r squared.
pages.name: Wedges into a rectangle

pages.text: Cut a circle into wedges and lay them top to tail. They make a rough rectangle πr long, half of the way round, 2πr, and one [[radius]] tall. So the area is πr × r = πr².

pages.alt: A circle inside the four squares on its radius, the one above the radius split into 1 centimetre squares. The radius is 2 centimetres; the square on it holds 4 of those 1 centimetre squares, and the circle covers 12.57 square centimetres, pi times the square on its radius. That is 4 times the area at a radius of 1 centimetre, 3.14 square centimetres.

pages.alt: The end of a solid round wire, 2 millimetres across. Its radius is 1 millimetre, with the square on it drawn; pi r squared is pi times 1 squared equals 3.14 square millimetres.

pages.task: This solid round wire is 2 mm across. What is its [[cross-section]]?
pages.why: Halve the diameter first, so r = 1 mm. The cross-section is πr² = π × 1² = 3.14 mm².

pages.alt: Two solid round wire ends: wire A, 2 millimetres across, and wire B, 4 millimetres across. The square on A's radius is one small square; the square on B's radius holds four of them. B has 12.57 square millimetres, 4 times A's 3.14.

pages.task: Solid round wire B is twice as wide across as wire A. How many times A's cross-section does it have?

pages.alt: A pipe's end: a circle of radius 5 centimetres. The hole, of radius 4 centimetres, is cut out and lifted away, leaving the ring. The hole is pi times 4 squared, 50.27 square centimetres. The ring is 78.54 minus 50.27, which is 28.27 square centimetres.
pages.name: A ring

pages.text: A pipe's end is a ring, an [[annulus]]. Its area is the whole circle less the hole. Work out each with πr², then take one from the other.

pages.alt: A pipe's end, a ring 12 centimetres across outside and 10 centimetres across inside. Halved, the radii are 6 and 5 centimetres. The hole, a circle of its own, is lifted out, and the ring is 113.10 minus 78.54, which is 34.56 square centimetres.
pages.name: The metal in a pipe
pages.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 340 222" width="340" style="fill:#1d1f22;stroke:none;stroke-width:1px;font-family:system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-weight:400;text-anchor:start" height="222"><style>.s0{stroke:#1d1f22;stroke-width:2.25px;stroke-linecap:round}.s1{stroke:#fff;stroke-width:3.25px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:middle;paint-order:stroke}</style><g><path d="M30 122a60 60 0 1 0 120 0a60 60 0 1 0 -120 0ZM40 122a50 50 0 1 0 100 0a50 50 0 1 0 -100 0Z" fill-rule="evenodd" style="fill:#d6e0eb;stroke:#1d1f22;stroke-width:2px"/><g><circle cx="250" cy="122" r="50" style="fill:#cfe8e4;stroke:#1d1f22;stroke-width:2px"/><line x1="250" y1="122" x2="300" y2="122" class="s0"/><circle cx="250" cy="122" r="3"/><text x="275" y="115" text-anchor="middle" class="s1">5 cm</text></g><g><line x1="90" y1="122" x2="30" y2="122" class="s0"/><circle cx="90" cy="122" r="3"/><text x="68" y="115" text-anchor="middle" class="s1">6 cm</text></g><g><text x="338" y="15" text-anchor="end" style="fill:#0b6a70;stroke:#fff;stroke-width:3.25px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">the metal ring</text><text x="338" y="38" text-anchor="end" style="stroke:#fff;stroke-width:5px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:20px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">113.10 − 78.54 = 34.56 cm²</text></g></g><g/></svg>
pages.task: A pipe is 12 cm across outside and 10 cm across inside. What is the area of its metal ring?
pages.why: Halve both, so the radii are 6 cm and 5 cm. The whole circle is π × 6² = 113.10 cm² and the hole is π × 5² = 78.54 cm², so the ring is 34.56 cm².

pages.task: A round shaft's end has an area of 28.27 cm². How wide across is it?
pages.why: Undo each step. 28.27 ÷ π = 9.00, which is r², so r = √9 = 3 cm. Across is 2 × 3 = 6 cm.

pages.alt: A cable drum's barrel, a circle of radius 30 centimetres, standing on the ground. It rolls once and its rim lays down a track 188.50 centimetres long, pi times 60 centimetres.
pages.name: Round the drum
pages.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 340 210" width="340" style="fill:#1d1f22;stroke:none;stroke-width:1px;font-family:system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif;font-size:16px;font-weight:400;text-anchor:start" height="210"><g><line x1="8" y1="200" x2="332" y2="200" style="stroke:#a9afb6;stroke-width:1.5px"/><line x1="46" y1="200" x2="284.76" y2="200" style="stroke:#1d1f22;stroke-width:3px;stroke-linecap:round"/><circle cx="284.76" cy="162" r="38" style="fill:none;stroke:#1d1f22;stroke-width:3px"/><circle cx="284.76" cy="200" r="4.5"/><g><text x="338" y="15" text-anchor="end" style="fill:#0b6a70;stroke:#fff;stroke-width:3.25px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:13px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">once round</text><text x="338" y="38" text-anchor="end" style="stroke:#fff;stroke-width:5px;stroke-linejoin:round;font-size:20px;font-weight:700;text-anchor:end;paint-order:stroke">2 × π × 30 = 188.50 cm</text></g></g><g/></svg>
pages.task: A cable drum's barrel has a radius of 30 cm. How far is it once round the barrel?
pages.why: With the radius, C = 2πr = 2 × π × 30 = 188.50 cm. That is the same as πd with d = 60 cm.

pages.task: Which has more cross-section, one solid wire 4 mm across or two solid wires 2 mm across?
pages.why: Twice the width makes four times the area. One 4 mm wire has 12.57 mm², and two 2 mm wires have 2 × 3.14 = 6.28 mm², half as much.

pages.task: A round hatch cover is 0.6 m across. What is its area?
pages.why: Halve the diameter, so r = 0.3 m. Then πr² = π × 0.3² = π × 0.09 = 0.28 m².
